text:
Buffalo is 8-7-4 with 20 points, and our numbers say that's about what the Sabres have earned: expected points of 20.3 against 20 actual. The problem is the direction. They're winless in three (0-2-1), outscored 15-6, and getting just 49% of the chances in that stretch. A loss to Tampa Bay closed a homestand, and Thursday's overtime loss in Chicago came on a Ryan Donato winner. Our playoff race has them at 27%.

The bright spot is the kids' line. Jack Quinn, Noah Ostlund and Zach Benson have taken 59% of the expected goals together and 65% of shot attempts, and Quinn is producing with his next contract already a topic in the coverage. Tage Thompson's move to a new position has him eyeing 50 goals, per the Buffalo Hockey Beat.

The worry is the blue line's top pair. Rasmus Dahlin and Mattias Samuelsson play the most minutes and sit at 49% of expected goals, while Owen Power and Olen Zellweger have been better on process but on the wrong end of the scoreboard (four goals for, seven against). Goals against are running about five above what the shots deserved, so the goaltending hasn't bailed them out.

For Lindy Ruff, watch whether the Quinn line keeps its minutes when Buffalo needs goals, because it has been their best answer.
headline: The Sabres sit level, and the slide is real
